title: Determining the Minimum Number of Virtual Networks for Different Coherence Protocols
problem: Cache coherence protocols conventionally determine virtual network (VN) requirements based on the longest chain of message dependencies. This approach is shown to be neither necessary nor sufficient for avoiding deadlock in systems with arbitrary interconnection network topologies and multiple directories.
motivation: Determining the actual minimum number of virtual networks is critical for designing efficient cache coherence protocols that avoid deadlock while minimizing network overhead and resource utilization.
method: The authors developed a formalism for modeling coherence protocols and their interactions with interconnection network queueing behavior. They created an algorithm that analyzes protocol message dependencies within the formal model to determine the minimum virtual networks required to provably prevent deadlock and generates optimal message-to-virtual-network mappings.
key_novelty: The paper demonstrates that conventional wisdom about VN requirements based on longest message dependency chains is incorrect and provides a formalism-based algorithm to compute the true minimum virtual networks needed.
contributions: Disproof that longest message dependency chain determines sufficient VN requirements
Formal model for coherence protocols and ICN queueing interactions
Algorithm to compute minimum virtual networks for deadlock avoidance
Method to generate optimal message type to virtual network mappings

metrics.other: Minimum virtual networks required; deadlock avoidance guarantee

limitations: Applicability to other protocol families and computational complexity of the algorithm not discussed
primary_theme: Minimum virtual network requirements for cache coherence
